# Divergence PATHS the conservation harness treats as report-only on a
# TRANSLATION lane (one whose ingress and egress dialects differ).
#
# Format: one `<ingress> <egress> <divergence-path>` triple per line.
#   ingress -- `IngressAdapter::id()` token (anthropic, openai,
#              openai-responses)
#   egress  -- egress lane token (anthropic-api, openai-compat,
#              bedrock-invoke, bedrock-converse, openai-responses, gemini)
#   path    -- the divergence path in the comparator's syntax
#              (`max_tokens`, `generationConfig`, `messages[0].role`)
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored.
#
# Keyed per LANE, not per path alone: a transform measured on one lane
# proves nothing on another, so a path excused here for one lane pair is
# still a finding on every other.
#
# THE SIGNAL IS CHANGE, NOT EMPTINESS. A translation lane never fails for
# diverging -- crossing a dialect boundary is what it does. It fails when a
# divergence appears on a path this file does not list, i.e. when the
# translation shape moved.
#
# Empty is LEGAL here, unlike in gated_lanes.txt, and the difference is
# deliberate: an empty gated set would downgrade every gated comparison to
# report-only (fail-open), whereas an empty baseline makes every
# translation divergence a failure (fail-closed). Emptiness is the strict
# end of this file's range.
#
# A MISSING file, however, is an error: an unreadable baseline is unknown,
# and an unknown baseline cannot adjudicate anything.
#
# Empty for now: the corpus carries no translation-lane fixture, so any
# entry here would be an unmeasured guess. Populated from a measured run
# the first time a translation-lane capture exists.
